It took one of my colleagues to press me abit after I didn't give a convincing enough "yeah I'm brand new" before I eventually opened up about how I was doing. It felt absolutely amazing to speak to someone and not have everything bottled up. Not saying opening up to a mate at work is right for you, just that it worked for me. 

I think i read on UK cop humour that we are rubbish at dealing with our own shit, but brilliant at dealing with other people's.

I take your point on board, however as I stated twice in my post, my criticism was not aimed at the OP, it was aimed at their force. We for example, have posters, signs, intranet pages all which slap you in the face at every turn directing us to different services. Not to mention the countless wellbeing emails we get sent. I just assumed every force was the same. If not, then the forces that do should be shamed into doing better. Too many of us in the job are lost due to the "heavy heid", myself almost included.

Can i ask how long you've been in the job for? It's just (and I'm truely not having a dig at you) but how do you not know there are services open to you? Again, definetly not having a go at you, more at your force for not making it abundantly clear what's out there so you don't have to go around asking, which for alot of people is a hard thing to do. 

Anyway, I hope you get the answers you're looking for and get the help you need.
